clue.text: How deranged, mad, obstinate and perverse!

indicators.note: mad suggests the preceding letters have gone crazy and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: An exclamation at someone behaving in a crazed, stubborn and contrary way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deranged' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'mad' does the shuffling of HOW DERANGED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wrong-headed clings stubbornly to a mistaken view, which is obstinate and contrary behaviour.

clue.text: Unofficial act we might deduce?

indicators.note: we might deduce invites the solver to work backwards from the result shown to the instruction that produced it

parts.note: the word act is what you get when the word cat runs wild, that is rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about what to infer from a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: WILD CAT read as an anagram instruction (CAT, wild) yields ACT. A wildcat strike is one not backed by the union.
explanation.definitionFit: A wildcat strike or action is unofficial, not authorised by the union.

clue.text: Obscure old memorial tablet with line missing

indicators.note: missing tells us that letter is absent from the tablet word

parts.note: a plaque is a commemorative tablet

explanation.surface: An ancient commemorative plaque has worn away a row of text, making it unreadable.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaque means hard to understand, so obscure in meaning.

clue.text: Jealous person in political organisation

parts.note: green with envy means jealous
party is a formal or legal word for a person, as in the guilty party

explanation.surface: An envious member of a political group.
explanation.definitionFit: The Green Party is an environmentalist political party.

clue.text: Is inclined to reject leader's aims

indicators.note: reject leader's says the first letter of the inclined word is thrown out

parts.note: tends means is inclined to

explanation.surface: Someone tends to dismiss the boss's goals.
explanation.definitionFit: Ends are goals or purposes, as in means to an end, so aims.

clue.text: Food shop that's odd has one in a state of agitation

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a shop selling prepared foods

indicators.note: in puts the numeral inside the odd word

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A strange delicatessen drives one into a frenzy.
explanation.definitionFit: Delirium is a disturbed state of frenzied excitement or confusion.

clue.text: German article collecting water that facilitates drying process

indicators.note: collecting means the article gathers the water inside itself

parts.note: der is the German masculine definite article
rain is falling water

explanation.surface: A German item that gathers water helps dry things off.
explanation.definitionFit: A drainer is a rack or board where washed dishes are left to drip dry.

clue.text: Gather after expected time having come to mountain pass

indicators.note: having come to places the tardy piece directly after the pass, so it follows it

parts.note: a col is a pass between mountain peaks
late means arriving past the due time

explanation.surface: Someone collects things after turning up late at an alpine pass.
explanation.definitionFit: To collate is to gather and arrange sheets or information together.

clue.text: Unruly local teens gathered round end of street in cluster

indicators.note: gathered round means the rearranged letters surround the letter taken from street
unruly means disorderly, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the words as written, used as fodder

indicators.note: end of means the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Rowdy youngsters from the area crowd round the end of the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unruly' rearranges LOCAL TEENS; 'gathered round' puts the last letter of street, T, inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: To constellate is to gather into a cluster, like stars forming a group.

clue.text: University lecturers are briefly entertained by theologian who isn't bright?

indicators.note: entertained by means held inside, as a guest is hosted within a home

parts.note: DD stands for Doctor of Divinity, a theologian
L is an abbreviation for lecturer, doubled here for the plural

indicators.note: briefly asks for the word before it to be cut short by its final letter

parts.note: the word are as written, before shortening

explanation.surface: Academic staff at a university are hosted by a divine who is not very clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops the final letter of 'are'; 'lecturers' doubles the usual single-letter abbreviation for a lecturer to make it plural.
explanation.definitionFit: A dullard is a slow-witted person, one who is not bright.

clue.text: Mad man tries to shoot — weapon removal is the answer

indicators.note: to shoot is here taken loosely as to send flying, scattering the letters

explanation.surface: A lunatic attempts to fire, and the solution is to take away the guns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder MAD MAN TRIES; 'to shoot' does the shuffling.
explanation.definitionFit: Disarmament is the taking away or reduction of weapons.

clue.text: No performance in church for this piece of music

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in places the act inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a turn is a performer's act or routine

explanation.surface: A piece written for an occasion when church performances are banned.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturne is a short dreamy composition, typically for piano, so it is a musical piece.

clue.text: Rows initiated by cold obsessive folk

indicators.note: initiated by means the rows piece is started off by the cold letter

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on a tap
ranks are rows, as of soldiers

explanation.surface: Arguments sparked by chilly fanatics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' reads as quarrels, but it means lines, as in ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: Cranks are eccentric people fixated on one idea, hence obsessive folk.

clue.text: Make quiet argument that mathematicians can't refute?

definitions.meaning: to insulate a room against noise so it is silent inside
a watertight demonstration of a theorem, reading the answer's two halves separately

explanation.definitionFit: Soundproofing stops noise getting in or out, and a sound proof is a valid logical demonstration.

clue.text: Thanks repeated and so long

indicators.note: repeated tells us to write the thanks word twice in a row

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: Saying thank you twice before saying goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Ta-ta is a casual British farewell, the same as so long or goodbye.

clue.text: Fellow wanting work, right manipulative type

parts.note: a man is a fellow
oeuvre is a body of work, or a single work

explanation.surface: A man in need of a job turns out to be a schemer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' looks like a deletion signal, but it is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A manoeuvrer is someone who schemes and steers events to their advantage, a manipulator.

clue.text: One that's enormous as a hit-maker

definitions.meaning: an informal word for something huge, a whopper
one who wallops, that is hits hard

explanation.definitionFit: Walloper is slang for something very big, and literally it is a person who wallops or strikes.

clue.text: Criticising innocent person — a police trap?

parts.note: a lamb is a meek and innocent person
a sting is an undercover police operation to catch criminals

explanation.surface: Attacking a blameless person, as if it were an entrapment operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambasting means berating harshly, a strong form of criticising.

clue.text: Motorway arrest with one having top speed in that vehicle

parts.note: the M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds, written MI

indicators.note: in places the numeral and speed symbol inside the arrest word

parts.note: nab is informal for arrest
I is the Roman numeral for one
c is the symbol for the speed of light, the fastest possible

explanation.surface: A speeding driver is pulled over on the motorway in some car.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's first full motorway, read as MI; c, the speed of light, is the top speed there is.
explanation.definitionFit: A minicab is a private hire car, a type of vehicle booked by phone.

clue.text: Military commander has some bag handlers

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An army officer has porters to carry his luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: An agha is an Ottoman or Turkish title; 'has' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Agha was a title for a military commander or chief officer in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Mr Cooper has managed to get locked in storehouse

indicators.note: get locked in means the managed word is shut inside the name

parts.note: Gary Cooper was the Hollywood film star
ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: An actor manages to be shut inside a barn.
explanation.definitionFit: A granary is a storehouse for threshed grain.

clue.text: Dupe the childminder?

definitions.meaning: an easy target or someone easily fooled, a sitting duck
short for babysitter, a person who looks after children

explanation.definitionFit: A sitter is an easy target or gullible person, and also short for babysitter.

clue.text: A service provided by ancient headmaster of yesteryear

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, one of the armed services
old means ancient

explanation.surface: An elderly person offers some kind of help.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Arnold was the famous nineteenth-century headmaster of Rugby School in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Arnold, the reforming head of Rugby School, is a celebrated headmaster from the past.

clue.text: Green crop either side of river is stuff that's wasted

indicators.note: either side of means the crop word wraps round the river, one part on each side

parts.note: silage is green fodder crop stored for animal feed
the Po is the main river of northern Italy

explanation.surface: Fodder growing on both banks of a river is rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoilage is material that has gone bad and been wasted.

clue.text: Every shrubbery has two such insects

definitions.text: Every shrubbery has two such insects

parts.words: Every shrubbery has two such insects
parts.note: the word shrubbery contains two of the letter B, and every two of the letter E, spelt out as words, which also name buzzing insects

explanation.surface: A claim that each garden bush harbours a pair of buzzing creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: Spell out the letter B in the plural and it sounds like the insects; shrubbery holds two of that letter.
explanation.definitionFit: These insects are the honey-making buzzers, and also the plural of the letter B.

clue.text: One getting away, see, disguised around head

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the headland word
disguised means the letters are rearranged to hide their original form

parts.note: the word see as written, used as fodder
a cape is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A fugitive, look, wears something over their head as a disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is not the definition's 'look' here but fodder; 'disguised' rearranges it and 'around' wraps the result about the headland word.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapee is someone who has broken free, one getting away.

clue.text: Unfashionable actors in the wilderness?

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
the cast is the group of actors in a production

explanation.surface: A troupe of players no longer in vogue is sent out into the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an adjectival phrase: being in the wilderness means being rejected and excluded, as an outcast is.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cast out from society is figuratively exiled, in the political wilderness.

clue.text: They may make brief drops, ending with 'takeaway'

definitions.text: They may make brief drops, ending with 'takeaway'

indicators.note: make suggests these letters can be made into something else by rearranging
ending with means the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Raptors swoop down briefly and then carry off their meal.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIEF DROPS rearranged makes BIRDSOFPRE, and the last letter of takeaway adds Y; the whole clue describes hawks stooping and carrying off prey.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawks and eagles swoop down in short dives and carry away their catch.
